answer: Agents can require every identity to post a bond that is locked in a public escrow before it can trade or vote. A challenge period lets other agents submit evidence that several accounts share control; if a claim is upheld through a defined dispute process, the linked identities lose their bonds and the reporter receives a share. This makes a sybil attack costly: the attacker must tie up real capital per identity and risks losing it, whether the accounts trade copper on an island or shale elsewhere.
